title: Tor one and a minimal graded presentation
statement: Let k be a field and S=k[x_0,x_1] with total-degree grading [def-sc-p1-standard], let S_+=(x_0,x_1), and let N be a finitely generated graded S-module [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Let q:F\to N be a finite graded free presentation such that the induced map F/S_+F\to N/S_+N is an isomorphism, and put K=ker(q). Then there is a natural isomorphism Tor_1^S(N,k)\cong K/S_+K. Consequently Tor_1^S(N,k)=0 implies K/S_+K=0.

source.place: proof, graded Nakayama criterion applied to K_2

proof.text: The sequence 0 \to K \to F \to N \to 0 is short exact by the definition of K and the presentation. Apply the low-degree Tor exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-tor-long-exact-first-variable] with R=S and second variable k. It gives an exact sequence Tor_1^S(F,k) \to Tor_1^S(N,k) \to K tensor_S k \to F tensor_S k \to N tensor_S k \to 0, natural in the second variable.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M0 (low-degree long exact sequence of Tor)

proof.text: The module F is free, so Tor_1^S(F,k)=0 by [lem-sc-p1-tor-free-vanishing]. With k=S/S_+, the isomorphism (S/S_+)\otimes_S M \to M/S_+M, \bar r\otimes x\mapsto rx mod S_+M, of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] (1), composed with the swap M\otimes_S k\cong k\otimes_S M, identifies M\otimes_S k with M/S_+M for M=K,F,N; by its explicit formula this identification commutes with the maps induced by S-linear maps M\to M'. Under it the map F\otimes_S k \to N\otimes_S k is the stated isomorphism F/S_+F \to N/S_+N, so exactness forces the map K\otimes_S k \to F\otimes_S k to be zero and identifies Tor_1^S(N,k) naturally with K\otimes_S k, hence with K/S_+K.

source.place: Algebra, Section Tag 00LY and Lemma Tag 00M0, Tor computed from a free resolution and the exact sequence

proof.text: Thus Tor_1^S(N,k) is naturally isomorphic to K/S_+K. Any isomorphism carries the zero module to the zero module, so Tor_1^S(N,k)=0 implies K/S_+K=0.
